extraction.Name: Joseph Brown and Alice Brown
extraction.Tribe/Reservation: Bennett County, South Dakota (Pine Ridge area)
extraction.Refused/Protested: the son, William D. Brown, did not desire the patent, as he did not want to pay taxes; but Joseph Brown was told that, if it was not accepted, and the taxes paid, the land would be taxed just the same, and later sold for taxes, so he accepted the patent for his son
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: as far as they are concerned, this land has never been mortgaged or sold
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: no taxes were ever paid on this land; in 1922, the land was sold for taxes then due and delinquent for the year 1921, at tax sale by the Treasurer of said County to Bennett County, purchaser
extraction.Age: Joseph Brown: 59 years old; Alice Brown: 58 years old
extraction.Occupation/Income: Mrs. Alice Brown receives United States Army insurance amounting to $57.50 per month; Joseph Brown and his wife Alice each receive $15.00 per month pension money
extraction.NOTES: Affidavit sworn March 29, 1929. The allotment belonged to their son William D. Brown, who died February 7, 1919, in Germany of influenza while serving in the United States Army. Son's Army insurance was drawn in favor of his mother Alice Brown. The 160-acre allotment (SE1, Sec. 6, T. 36N., R. 36W., 6th P.M., South Dakota) was never probated; deponents were informed probate would prevent putting it back in trust. They desired to have the allotment put back in trust. Land leased to Dewey Dirks for $64.00 per annum. Deponents furnished four soldier boys for the World War. Document includes a newspaper clipping from the Martin Messenger regarding a Notice to Owner Before Tax Deed Shall Expire. The forced patent was sent to the father Joseph Brown, who refused to sign for it at first.
